bottleneck: Deep brain stimulation helps Parkinson's and other disorders, but targeting is approximate: electrodes stimulate cubic millimeters containing millions of neurons of many types, and current spread cannot be confined to the intended circuit. Programming the device is trial-and-error across thousands of parameter combinations, and side effects arise from stimulating adjacent pathways — speech, mood, cognition. Precision neuromodulation needs cell-type specificity that electricity fundamentally cannot provide.
current_state: Directional leads and imaging-guided targeting improve accuracy incrementally, but DBS remains a blunt electrical intervention tuned by hand over months of clinic visits.
title: DBS stimulation too coarse for circuit precision
why_it_blocks: Psychiatry and neurology need to modulate specific circuits, not bathe brain regions in current. Without precision, DBS stays limited to a few disorders where blunt stimulation happens to help, leaving most circuit disorders untreated.
